subject: Mermaid Fidelity capability assessments with basis `model-concept` ("a reviewed view declares the concept absent from the native model", unified/mermaid-fidelity/outcome-kinds.ts): every distinct reason in results/release/mermaid-fidelity.json assessmentReasons, per candidate, checked against the installed candidate artifacts of the 0.4.0 campaign (prepared artifacts: the campaign's community-prepared.json; packages under node_modules/.cache/unified-community/ and node_modules/.cache/fidelity-bridges/). Follows the capability review (fidelity-capability-review-2026-11-14.json), which probed class notes, edge ids, participant/actor kinds, C4 wrap and the git checked-out branch and left the rest unprobed.
baseline: results/release/mermaid-fidelity.json (the 2026-11-14 jsdom campaign): baselineCallbacks counts, per project, the callbacks whose capability assessment carried that reason.
method: Each concept was probed by running the candidate's own public parser, through the runtime's native parse path exactly as the views receive it (runtime.ts probeNative, scripts/fidelity-probe.ts; batch runner in the review's scratch tools), on sources that write the concept with unique marker tokens (probeSources below), then searching the native model for the markers and comparing models of sources that differ only in the concept. Where a model carried the concept, the installed source or type declarations were read to establish the encoding (cited file:line). Confirmed: the native model does not carry the value (dropped, folded into display text, merged with another written form, or rejected). Disproved: the native model carries it; the view now reads it from the model. Not decidable: the probe cannot settle the claim (none in this review).

concepts.evidence: agentic-mermaid 0.5.6 parseRegisteredMermaid keeps accDescr in the result's meta.accessibility.descr for flowchart, ER, gantt and radar bodies; the runtime hands it to the views as accessibilityDescription (runtime.ts nativeParse, agentic branch). Probes return accessibilityDescription: 'ACCDSC' for all four (and for the upstream erDiagram.spec.js accessible-title source: 'this graph is about stuff'). ER uses the editing model, since 0.5.6's agent-core exports no parseErDiagram.
concepts.action: Views read raw.accessibilityDescription (misc.mjs flowchart, ER editing branch and ganttGetters; gitgraph.mjs agenticRadar), Mermaid's '' when the meta field is unwritten.

A class with a defined class (`class C:::pink` / classDef pink) stays unsupported: Mermaid merges the classDef into styles in statement order, and the model keeps className, classDefs and style apart (measured: the two classDiagram-styles.spec.js callbacks that test this merge).

The model drops a written `animate: false` (e2@{ animate: false } leaves no flag, and e3@{ animate: true } followed by e3@{ animate: false } keeps true), so an edge without the flag is declared absent for that edge alone; Crafter keeps the declaration.

Frankenmermaid labels 'FILEX :::CLASSX', 'DIRX/', '"deep.js" icon(ICONX)' (annotations and trailing slash stay in the name); nodes keep no indentation.
wardley_meta keeps width, height, points, marks and stage bands (a laid-out drawing).
`rule = sequence(terminal("a"))` gives definition { type: 'terminal', value: 'a' } in merman-cli, Pele and Bezel, the same as `rule = terminal("a")`.

Pele and Bezel keep the usecase database maps (actors, useCases, systemBoundaries, relationships, classDefs) plus source and statement spans, not Mermaid's normalized AST node/edge/group/class tables (deriving them would compute Mermaid's normalization); merman-cli keeps nodes and relationships with no source or spans.

merman-cli 0.10.0 agentflow output is the semantic model: no view hint for `pipeline@{ view: "collapsed" }`, no icon / shape metadata (ICONX absent), no element source positions, connectors listed apart from vertices, no vertex record for a container id.

bridgeFallbacks.verdict: replaced by the candidate's own answer
bridgeFallbacks.evidence: mermaid-rs-renderer 0.3.1 src/parser.rs:58-62 parse_mermaid (the public entry the mmdr CLI uses) bails 'unknown or missing Mermaid diagram header' when detect_diagram_kind (parser.rs:109-210, private) finds none, and detect_diagram_kind returns Flowchart when a first line looks like flowchart edges. For agentflow, railroad (all notations), treeview, usecase, cynefin, ishikawa, wardley and venn sources it returns a Flowchart graph; for info and eventmodeling it bails with no header.
bridgeFallbacks.action: bridges/mmdr/src/main.rs: every family but Mermaid's cross-family <shared> request goes to parse_mermaid; a graph of another kind is 'mmdr detected this source as Flowchart, not <family>', no header is mmdr's own message, and a rejection of a source for a family its DiagramKind lacks is 'mmdr declined this source (...)' (never that family's syntax error). All three are NATIVE_OBSERVED / bridge-relayed candidate messages: native-unsupported. No pass/fail logic changed.
bridgeFallbacks.remaining: 19 callbacks keep 'mmdr has no <shared> parser' (a capability assessment: Mermaid's own cross-family detection, which SHARED_REQUEST classifies as an assessment whoever words it).

bridgeFallbacks.verdict: replaced by the candidate's own answer
bridgeFallbacks.evidence: termaid 0.12.0 termaid/__init__.py parse(source) (public: 'Auto-detects diagram type (flowchart or state diagram)') calls parse_state_diagram for a stateDiagram header and parse_flowchart for anything else; its renderer (_render_canvas) draws every header it does not dispatch the same way, as the capability review found. For c4, radar, requirement, agentflow, railroad, treeview, usecase, cynefin, eventmodeling, ishikawa, wardley, venn and info sources termaid.parse() reads the source as a flowchart.
bridgeFallbacks.action: bridges/termaid.py: a family with no per-family parser (other than <shared>) is answered by termaid.parse(); the bridge observes which of its two parsers it dispatched to (wrapping the module's parse_flowchart / parse_state_diagram for that call) and replies {unsupported: 'termaid parsed this source as <kind>, not <family>', native: true}: native-unsupported. No pass/fail logic changed.

measured.run: mermaid:fidelity --workers 1 (jsdom), control and the twelve affected candidates recollected in full (all 352 selected files, 7,346 reference-qualified callbacks each); agentic-mermaid recollected again after its edge-animate and class-styles readings were narrowed. Compared per callback (file, name, ordinal) with the published raw run of the 0.4.0 campaign. Kinds: P passed, NF native-failure, NU native-unsupported, CA capability-assessment, AL adapter-limitation.
notes: Every move is out of capability-assessment; no callback moved out of passed or native-failure, and none moved into capability-assessment.

zombie-mermaid: 4 newly known callbacks fail on the candidate's own values: `buzz foo["batman"]` leaves foo unaliased in its model (2, erDiagram.spec.js; Mermaid: alias 'batman'), and its note text keeps line breaks as newlines where Mermaid keeps '
' (2 inline snapshots, stateDiagram-v2.spec.js).

The six disproved subgraph-classes readings moved no callback: their one test (flowDb.spec.ts repeated subgraph ids) also reads the subgraph's label type, a confirmed absent concept for those models (Frankenmermaid, agentic-mermaid, Crafter, zombie-mermaid, beautiful-mermaid, ascii-mermaid), so it stays a capability assessment under that reason.

agentic-mermaid's first collection with the edge-animate and class-styles readings fixed made 3 native failures that came from the view, not the candidate (an `animate: false` the model drops read as unset; classDef styles Mermaid merges into a class read as empty); both readings were narrowed (declared absent where the model cannot tell) and agentic-mermaid recollected: 25 capability assessments became passes, no native failures.
